pr_title: Restructure and refine the noise module
pr_body:
This PR is a follow-up to #56718 aiming to improve/refine the noise module and incorporate some of the feedback paired with a couple of bugfixes:

- Make interface methods and FastNoiseLite functions const
- Add mipmap generation toggleable with property (significantly improves quality, see demo picture below)
-  Move property color_ramp to NoiseTexture, so it can be used with other noise generators (in general, it makes more sense like that because it has nothing to do with the noise generator)
-  Move property in_3d_space to NoiseTexture (makes more sense there imo, since it was only used for creating 2d images; it is now a parameter of the get_image/get_seamless_image functions)
    -   Fix transparency blending for seamless textures
-  Change the default cellular distance function from CELL_VALUE to DISTANCE (as it is more common)
-  Initialize all primitive variables in the header and restructure the constructor of the FastNoiseLite resource so that emit_changed() and notify_property_list_changed() won't be called in it
- Some minor code style improvements, fix typo in fractal_ping_pong_strength and restructure *_bind_methods() to be more consistent with the rest of the codebase
-  Fix color_ramp removal not updating texture
-  Move the get_image implementation to noise.cpp as it just uses the interface methods and nothing specific to FastNoiseLite. Noise generators can still overwrite it, but the standard implementation should be sufficient in most cases.
- Add a general Noise resource preview plugin (quite essential when using the Noise resource directly without NoiseTexture for e.g. procedural world generation, etc.)
	- Toggleable "in 3d space" preview option (saved individually per resource)
	- Uses a NoiseTexture internally, so the noise generation happens on a thread allowing for smooth editing and direct feedback
- Fix domain warp noise always using seed 0
- Fix noise offset step size set to 1, effectively only allowing integers for each component when set via the inspector

Demo with materials which only use noise textures:
![dem1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50084500/163697168-06017767-b9ab-45ef-a107-81038aac3743.png)

Demo of the noise preview:
![noise_preview](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50084500/163697290-d4e6f606-cb58-4e4d-8051-537bae88ea45.gif)

There are still some features left I would like to add, but those are better addressed in another PR.

*Bugsquad edit: This closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/36675.*

issue_context.title: Vulkan: Mipmaps aren't generated automatically for a NoiseTexture applied to a StandardMaterial3D
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** Git https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/e4bc16b7b6a7a9354e6037cb571de934a8ec1430

**OS/device including version:** Fedora 31, NVIDIA 440.44, GeForce GTX 1080

**Issue description:** Mipmaps aren't being generated when applying a NoiseTexture in a 3D environment, which makes the texture grainy at a distance. This doesn't happen with ImageTexture. Interestingly, enabling anisotropic filtering on the texture *slightly* improves the appearance, but not by much.

**Steps to reproduce:** Create a MeshInstance and a StandardMaterial3D. Assign a NoiseTexture with OpenSimplexNoise to the material's Albedo property. Compare the result with an ImageTexture.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/75608929-3aa35180-5b04-11ea-807a-dafe562ae984.png)

**Minimal reproduction project:** [test_mipmap.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4270376/test_mipmap.zip)
comments: Confirmed in the current master branch (201d5a7fc53c041e011ad7a79b805f5989216d28).

Did it work in 3.2?

![godot_noise_texture_mipmaps](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17108460/96911379-729f4080-14a9-11eb-8a6a-ea25d88f035e.png)

See https://github.com/Xrayez/godot/commit/8ae82725849584de944f64f49183d5c8163ac871.

> Compare the result with an ImageTexture.

The MRP doesn't generate `ImageTexture` dynamically, but instead uses `StreamTexture`, which is imported with mipmaps to be generated by default. `NoiseTexture` is generated procedurally, but there's no texture flags to configure this in `master`.

~~@Xrayez The NoiseTexture definitely appears smoothed out in the distance on your screenshot. Compare it to the screenshot in OP :slightly_smiling_face:~~

**Edit:** Nevermind, I read your comment again. This is something we need to modify in both `3.2` and `master`.

No, I was just curious whether it used to work in 3.2. 🙂

Just tested, it's not an issue in 3.2. Texture flags were removed in `master`, but available in 3.2:

![godot_noise_texture_flags](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17108460/96912454-16d5b700-14ab-11eb-9933-38171652e73f.png)

I don't know how it works internally.

**Test project**:
[test_mipmap-3.2.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5424829/test_mipmap-3.2.zip)

review_comments:
```suggestion
			Color ramp_color = color_ramp->get_color_at_offset(pixel_color.r);
```

Does it need to use luminance here, or can it use the raw noise value? Before this PR it used the raw noise value, whereas `get_luminance()` does some kind of color space conversion.

If you do change this then the code from the next comment will need to be updated, because it includes this line with `get_luminance()`.

I think get_luminance calculates the perceived brightness of a pixel, so for a grayscale image where r=g=b the computed value is the same as the r component. However, if a noise library generates an image in color all channels are included with get_luminance().

You're right, the code you suggested would be slightly faster, but the problem is the lack of flexibility. (a Noise resource could generate a float texture). NoiseTexture should be able to handle all image formats because it has no information about which format `get_image` or `get_seamless_image` returns.
